messages:
joel: Heads-up: multiple new users report unhelpful SDK errors. Example: JS throws Error("request failed") and Go prints Err: "bad request" with no machine-readable code. Friction during onboarding.

rachel: Yep saw this in onboarding-qa. Our API returns structured error payloads (code + message + meta) but clients flatten. That makes retry logic and user-facing messages brittle.

alex: Proposal: define a canonical error namespace and escape-hatch fields. e.g. error.code = "redwood.rate.limit_exceeded" and status = 429, details = {retry_after: 30}. Keep message human-friendly.

joel: We should be non-breaking initially: add .code and .status fields to existing Error objects in JS/Python/Go while keeping message text identical. Then introduce typed subclasses in a major later.

rachel: Also add a helper util: `isRateLimit(err)` in SDKs to abstract checks and handle older/no-code cases. Docs should include a mapping table:
- 401 -> redwood.auth.invalid_credentials
- 403 -> redwood.auth.forbidden
- 429 -> redwood.rate.limit_exceeded
- 400 -> redwood.validation.invalid_input
- 422 -> redwood.validation.unprocessable
- 500/503 -> redwood.server.internal_error

alex: Example JS usage: `if (err.code === 'redwood.rate.limit_exceeded') { // backoff } else if (err.status === 401) { // refresh token }` Fallback: `if (!err.code && /quota/i.test(err.message)) { /* legacy */ }`

joel: Go SDK sketch:
```go
type RedwoodError struct {
  Msg string
  Code string
  Status int
  Details map[string]interface{}
}
func (e *RedwoodError) Error() string { return e.Msg }
```

rachel: Action items:
- rachel: open RFC (GH link: github.com/redwoodinc/repo/issues/xxx) with canonical codes and mapping table
- alex: implement non-breaking .code/.status in JS + helper util; add unit tests
- joel: update sample-apps to check err.code first, then err.status, then message regex for compatibility
- build-bot: run CI on sample-apps after changes

build-bot: sample-apps/edge-service PR #432: tests passed, e2e flaky test skipped with note.

alex: Timeline: land additive fields in next minor (v2.5.0), publish migration guide and code snippets; aim for typed subclasses in v3.0 with clear deprecation schedule.

rachel: Important: update error docs and include best-practice snippets for languages we officially support. Avoid encouraging substring parsing.

joel: Thanks team. I'll shepherd the RFC and coordinate with docs for clear examples. :thumbsup:
